paragraphs.sourceText: Some people borrow money and “forget” to pay it back.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有些人借钱后“忘记”还钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: Large loans are seldom the issue; they are usually treated as business 26 , with the terms spelled out on paper. But many women suffer 27 over problems like Carol’s “My friend Ginny is always 28 cash,” she says. “I hate to recall how often I’ve ‘loaned’ her a dollar or two for a drink or a movie. Each loan is so small I’d feel really cheap making a big deal out of it; still, I do 29 the fact that she never pays me back.

Carol admits to being “too 30 or something” to demand repayment, but she has resolved to stop lending money to Ginny. The last time she asked for five dollars to pay for her dry cleaning, I just told her I couldn’t 31 it.”

Another woman suggests a bolder 32 . “When somebody refuses to repay a loan, I 33 by requesting one myself,” she says. “ ‘I left home without my wallet,’ I’ll say. ‘Can you lend me enough to cover lunch?’ Then, when the money is safely in hand, I am struck by a sudden 34 . ‘Why, this is exactly the amount I loaned you last week! How 35 ! Now you won’t have to repay me!’” She says it works like a charm.

Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: For many Americans, 2013 ended with an unusually bitter cold spell. Late November and December 36 early snow and bone-chilling temperatures in much of the country, part of a year when, for the first time in two 37 ,record-cold days will likely turn out to have outnumbered record-warm ones. But the U. S. was the exception ：November was the warmest ever 38 , and current data indicates that 2013 is likely to have been the fourth hottest year on record.
Enjoy the snow now, because 39 are good that 2014 will be even hotter, perhaps the hottest year since records have been kept. That’s because, scientists are predicting, 2014 will be an El Nino year.

El Nino, Spanish for “the child”, 40 when surface ocean waters in the southern Pacific become abnormally warm. So large is the Pacific, covering 30% of the planet’s surface, that the 41 energy generated by its warming is enough to touch off a series of weather changes around the world. El Ninos are 42 with abnormally dry conditions in Southeast Asia and Australia. They can lead to extreme rain in parts of North and South America, even as southern Africa 43 dry weather. Marine life may be affected too：El Ninos can 44 the rising of the cold, nutrient-rich(营养丰富的）water that supports large fish 45 , and the unusually warm ocean temperatures can destroy coral （珊瑚）.

Directions ：In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. How to Eat Well
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡上标记相应的字母来回答问题 2. 如何吃得好

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Why do so many Americans eat tons of processed food, the stuff that is correctly called junk (垃圾）and should really carry warning labels?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 为什么这么多美国人吃大量的加工食品，这些东西被正确地称为垃圾（垃圾），并且真的应该贴上警告标签？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) It’s not because fresh ingredients are hard to come by. Supermarkets offer more variety than ever, and there are over four times as many farmers, markets in the U. S. as there were 20 years ago. Nor is it for lack of available information. There are plenty of recipes （食谱）how-to videos and cooking classes available to anyone who has a computer, smartphone or television. If anything, the information is overwhelming.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 这并不是因为新鲜食材很难获得。超市提供的商品种类比以往任何时候都多，美国的农贸市场数量是 20 年前的四倍多。也不是因为缺乏可用信息。有大量的食谱（食谱）教学视频和烹饪课程可供拥有电脑、智能手机或电视的任何人使用。如果有的话，信息是压倒性的。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) And yet we aren’t cooking. If you eat three meals a day and behave like most Americans, you probably get at least a third of your daily calories (卡路里）outside the home. Nearly two thirds of us grab fast food once a week, and we get almost 25% of our daily calories from snacks. So we’re eating out or taking in，and we don’t sit down—or we do, but we hurry.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 但我们还没做饭。如果你一天吃三顿饭，并且表现得像大多数美国人一样，那么你可能至少有三分之一的每日卡路里是在外面获得的。我们中近三分之二的人每周吃一次快餐，而我们每天的卡路里几乎有 25% 来自零食。所以我们在外面吃饭或在外面吃饭，我们不会坐下来——或者我们坐下来，但我们很快。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Shouldn’t preparing—and consuming—food be a source of comfort, pride, health, well-being, relaxation, sociability? Something that connects us to other humans? Why would we want to outsource （外包）this basic task, especially when outsourcing it is so harmful?
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 准备和消费食物难道不应该成为舒适、自豪、健康、幸福、放松和社交的源泉吗？有什么东西可以将我们与其他人联系起来？为什么我们要外包这个基本任务，尤其是当外包如此有害时？

paragraphs.sourceText: E) When I talk about cooking, I’m not talking about creating elaborate dinner parties or three-day science projects. I’m talking about simple, easy, everyday meals. My mission is to encourage green hands and those lacking time or money to feed themselves. That means we need modest, realistic expectations, and we need to teach people to cook food that’s good enough to share with family and friends.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 当我谈论烹饪时，我并不是在谈论精心策划的晚宴或为期三天的科学项目。我说的是简单、轻松的日常饮食。我的使命是鼓励新手和那些缺乏时间或金钱养活自己的人。这意味着我们需要适度、现实的期望，我们需要教人们烹饪出足以与家人和朋友分享的美味食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Perhaps a return to real cooking needn’t be far off. A recent Harris poll revealed that 79% of Americans say they enjoy cooking and 30% “love it”; 14% admit to not enjoying kitchen work and just 7% won’t go near the stove at all. But this doesn’t necessarily translate to real cooking, and the result of this survey shouldn’t surprise anyone : 52% of those 65 or older cook at home five or more times per week; only a third of young people do.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 也许回归真正的烹饪并不遥远。最近的哈里斯民意调查显示，79% 的美国人表示他们喜欢烹饪，30% 的人“喜欢它”； 14% 的人承认不喜欢厨房工作，只有 7% 的人根本不会靠近炉子。但这并不一定意味着真正的烹饪，这项调查的结果不应让任何人感到惊讶：65 岁或以上的老年人中，有 52% 每周在家做饭五次或以上；只有三分之一的年轻人这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Back in the 1950s most of us grew up in households where Mom cooked virtually every night. The intention to put a home-cooked meal on the table was pretty much universal. Most people couldn’t afford to do otherwise.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 早在 20 世纪 50 年代，我们大多数人都是在妈妈几乎每晚做饭的家庭中长大的。把一顿家常饭菜摆上餐桌的愿望几乎是普遍的。大多数人没有能力采取其他措施。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Although frozen dinners were invented in the 40s, their popularity didn’t boom until televisions became popular a decade or so later. Since then, packaged, pre-prepared meals have been what’s for dinner. The microwave and fast-food chains were the biggest catalyst (催化剂）, but the big food companies—which want to sell anything except the raw ingredients that go into cooking— made the home cook an endangered species.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 虽然冷冻晚餐是在 40 年代发明的，但直到大约十年后电视开始流行，它们才开始流行起来。从那时起，晚餐就变成了包装好的、预先准备好的饭菜。微波炉和快餐连锁店是最大的催化剂（催化剂），但大型食品公司——除了用于烹饪的原材料之外，什么都想卖——使家庭烹饪成为濒临灭绝的物种。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Still, I find it strange that only a third of young people report preparing meals at home regularly. Isn’t this the same crowd that rails against processed junk and champions craft cooking? And isn’t this the generation who say they’ve concerned about their health and the well-being of the planet? If these are truly the values of many young people, then their behavior doesn’t match their beliefs.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 不过，我觉得很奇怪的是，只有三分之一的年轻人表示定期在家做饭。这不就是反对加工垃圾和拥护手工烹饪的同一群人吗？难道这代人不是说他们关心自己的健康和地球的福祉吗？如果这些确实是许多年轻人的价值观，那么他们的行为就与他们的信仰不符。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) There have been half-hearted but well-publicized efforts by some food companies to reduce calories in their processed foods, but the Standard American Diet is still the polar opposite of the healthy, mostly plant-based diet that just about every expert says we should be eating. Considering that the government’s standards are not nearly ambitious enough, the picture is clear: by not cooking at home, we’re not eating the right things, and the consequences are hard to overstate.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 一些食品公司为减少加工食品中的卡路里做出了半心半意但广为人知的努力，但标准美国饮食仍然与健康的、以植物为主的饮食截然相反，几乎每个专家都认为我们应该吃这种饮食。考虑到政府的标准还不够雄心勃勃，情况就很清楚了：如果不在家做饭，我们就吃不到正确的东西，其后果怎么强调都不为过。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) To help quantify （量化）costs of a poor diet, I recently tried to estimate this impact in terms of a most famous food, the burger（汉堡包）. I concluded that the profit from burgers is more than offset（抵消）by the damage they cause in health problems and environmental harm.
paragraphs.translationZh: K）为了帮助量化不良饮食的成本，我最近尝试根据最著名的食物汉堡（汉堡包）来估计这种影响。我的结论是，汉堡带来的利润远远抵消了它们对健康问题和环境造成的损害。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Cooking real food is the best defense—not to mention that any meal you’ve likely to eat at home contains about 200 fewer calories than one you would eat in a restaurant.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 烹饪真正的食物是最好的防御——更不用说您在家吃的任何一顿饭都比在餐馆吃的饭菜少大约 200 卡路里。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) To those Americans for whom money is a concern, my advice is simple: Buy what you can afford, and cook it yourself. The common prescription is to primarily shop the grocery store, since that’s where fresh produce, meat and seafood, and dairy are. And to save money and still eat well you don’t need local, organic ingredients; all you need is real food. I’m not saying local food isn’t better; it is. But there is plenty of decent food in the grocery stores.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）对于那些关心钱的美国人，我的建议很简单：买你能买得起的东西，然后自己做饭。常见的做法是主要去杂货店购买，因为那里有新鲜农产品、肉类、海鲜和乳制品。为了省钱又吃得好，你不需要当地的有机原料；你所需要的只是真正的食物。我并不是说当地食物不好；而是说当地食物不好。这是。但杂货店里有很多像样的食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The other sections you should get to know are the frozen foods and the canned goods. Frozen produce is still produce; canned tomatoes are still tomatoes. Just make sure you’re getting real food without tons of added salt or sugar. Ask yourself, would Grandma consider this food? Does it look like something that might occur in nature? It’s pretty much common sense: you want to buy food, not unidentifiable foodlike objects.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 您应该了解的其他部分是冷冻食品和罐头食品。冷冻产品仍然是产品；罐装西红柿仍然是西红柿。只要确保您吃的是真正的食物，不添加大量的盐或糖。问问你自己，奶奶会考虑这个食物吗？它看起来像自然界中可能发生的事情吗？这几乎是常识：你想买食物，而不是无法识别的类似食物的物品。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) You don’t have to hit the grocery store daily, nor do you need an abundance of skill. Since fewer than half of Americans say they cook at an intermediate level and only 20% describe their cooking skills as advanced, the crisis is one of confidence. And the only remedy for that is practice. There’s nothing mysterious about cooking the evening meal. You just have to do a little thinking ahead and redefine what qualifies as dinner. Like any skill, cooking gets easier as you do it more; every time you cook, you advance your level of skills. Someday you won’t even need recipes. My advice is that you not pay attention to the number of steps and ingredients, because they can be deceiving.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 你不必每天都去杂货店，也不需要丰富的技能。由于只有不到一半的美国人表示自己的烹饪水平处于中级水平，只有 20% 的人称自己的烹饪技能较高，因此这场危机是一场信心危机。唯一的补救办法就是练习。做饭并没有什么神秘的。你只需要提前思考一下，重新定义什么才算是晚餐。就像任何技能一样，烹饪越多就会变得越容易。每次你做饭，你的技能水平都会提高。有一天你甚至不需要食谱。我的建议是你不要注意步骤和成分的数量，因为它们可能是骗人的。

paragraphs.sourceText: P) Time, I realize, is the biggest obstacle to cooking for most people. You must adjust your priorities to find time to cook. For instance, you can move a TV to the kitchen and watch your favorite shows while you’re standing at the sink. No one is asking you to give up activities you like, but if you’re watching food shows on TV, try cooking instead.
paragraphs.translationZh: P) 我意识到，对于大多数人来说，时间是做饭的最大障碍。你必须调整你的优先顺序才能找到做饭的时间。例如，您可以将电视移至厨房，然后站在水槽旁观看您喜爱的节目。没有人要求您放弃您喜欢的活动，但如果您正在电视上观看美食节目，请尝试做饭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Cooking benefits people in many ways and enables them to connect with one another.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 烹饪在很多方面使人们受益，并使他们能够相互联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Abundant information about cooking is available either online or on TV.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 网上或电视上提供了大量有关烹饪的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Young people do less cooking at home than the elderly these days.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 如今，年轻人在家做饭的次数比老年人少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Cooking skills can be improved with practice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 烹饪技巧可以通过练习来提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. In the mid-20th century, most families ate dinner at home instead of eating out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 20 世纪中叶，大多数家庭在家吃晚饭，而不是外出就餐。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Even those short of time or money should be encouraged to cook for themselves and their family.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 即使那些缺乏时间或金钱的人也应该被鼓励为自己和家人做饭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Eating food not cooked by ourselves can cause serious consequences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52、吃自己没有煮过的食物会造成严重的后果。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. To eat well and still save money, people should buy fresh food and cook it themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 为了吃得好又省钱，人们应该购买新鲜食物并自己做饭。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. We get a fairly large portion of calories from fast food and snacks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54.我们从快餐和零食中获取相当大部分的卡路里。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. The popularity of TV led to the popularity of frozen food.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55.电视的普及导致了冷冻食品的流行。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The wallet is heading for extinction. As a day-to-day essential，it will die off with the generation who read print newspapers. The kind of shopping—where you hand over notes and count out change in return—now happens only in the most minor of our retail encounters, like buying a bar of chocolate or a pint of milk from a comer shop. At the shops where you spend any real money, that money is increasingly abstracted. And this is more and more true, the higher up the scale you go. At the most cutting-edge retail stores—Victoria Beckham on Dover Street, for instance—you don’t go and stand at any kind of cash register when you decide to pay. The staff are equipped with iPads to take your payment while you relax on a sofa.
paragraphs.translationZh: 钱包正走向消亡。作为日常必需品，它将随着阅读纸质报纸的一代人而消失。这种购物方式——交出纸币并清点零钱作为回报——现在只发生在我们最微小的零售遭遇中，比如从街角商店购买一块巧克力或一品脱牛奶。在你花任何真钱的商店里，这些钱越来越抽象。级别越高，这一点就越正确。在最前沿的零售商店——例如多佛街的维多利亚·贝克汉姆——当你决定付款时，你不会走到任何收银台前。当您在沙发上休息时，工作人员会配备 iPad 来收取您的付款。

paragraphs.sourceText: Which is nothing more or less than excellent service, if you have the money. But across society, the abstraction of the idea of cash makes me uneasy. Maybe I’m just old-fashioned. But earning money isn’t quick or easy for most of us. Isn’t it a bit weird that spending it should happen in half a blink (眨眼）of an eye? Doesn’t a wallet—that time-honoured Friday-night feeling of pleasing, promising fatness—represent something that matters?
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你有钱的话，这无非就是优质的服务。但在整个社会，现金概念的抽象让我感到不安。也许我只是守旧。但对于我们大多数人来说，赚钱并不快也不容易。眨眼间就花掉了，这不是有点奇怪吗？钱包——周五晚上那种令人愉悦、有希望的肥胖的由来已久的感觉——难道不代表着重要的东西吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: But I’ll leave the economics to the experts. What bothers me about the death of the wallet is the change it represents in our physical environment. Everything about the look and feel of a wallet—the way the fastenings and materials wear and tear and loosen with age, the plastic and paper and gold and silver, and handwritten phone numbers and printed cinema tickets—is the very opposite of what our world is becoming. The opposite of a wallet is a smartphone or an iPad. The rounded edges, cool glass，smooth and unknowable as a pebble (鹅卵石）. Instead of digging through pieces of paper and peering into comers, we move our fingers left and right. No more counting out coins. Show your wallet, if you still have one. It may not be here much longer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但我会把经济学问题留给专家们。钱包的消亡让我困扰的是它给我们的物理环境带来的变化。钱包的外观和感觉的一切——紧固件和材料随着时间的推移而磨损和松动的方式，塑料和纸张，金和银，手写的电话号码和印刷的电影票——都与我们的世界正在发生的事情完全相反。钱包的反义词是智能手机或 iPad。圆润的边缘，凉爽的玻璃，像鹅卵石一样光滑且不可知。我们不再从纸片中挖掘并窥视角落，而是左右移动手指。不再数硬币。如果你还有钱包，请展示你的钱包。它可能不会在这里呆太久了。

paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Everybody sleeps, but what people stay up late to catch—or wake up early in order not to miss— varies by culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 每个人都会睡觉，但人们熬夜是为了赶上什么，或者早起是为了不错过什么——因文化而异。

paragraphs.sourceText: From data collected, it seems the things that cause us to lose the most sleep, on average, are sporting events, time changes, and holidays.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从收集的数据来看，平均而言，导致我们睡眠不足的因素是体育赛事、时间变化和假期。

paragraphs.sourceText: Around the world, people changed sleep patterns thanks to the start or end of daylight savings time, Russians, for example, began to wake up about a half-hour later each day after President Vladimir Putin shifted the country permanently to “winter time” starting on October 26.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在世界各地，由于夏令时的开始或结束，人们的睡眠模式发生了变化，例如，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)从10月26日开始将国家永久改为“冬令时”后，俄罗斯人开始每天晚起约半小时。

paragraphs.sourceText: Russia’s other late nights and early mornings generally correspond to public holidays. On New Year’s Eve, Russians have the world’s latest bedtime，hitting the hay at around 3:30 a.m.
paragraphs.translationZh: 俄罗斯的其他深夜和清晨通常与公共假期相对应。除夕夜，俄罗斯人的就寝时间是世界上最晚的，他们在凌晨 3:30 左右上床睡觉。

paragraphs.sourceText: 、Russians also get up an hour later on International Women’s Day, the day for treating and celebrating female relatives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 、俄罗斯人在国际妇女节这一天也会晚起一个小时，这一天是治疗和庆祝女性亲属的日子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Similarly, Americans, late nights, late mornings, and longest sleeps fall on three-day weekends. Canada got the least sleep of the year the night it beat Sweden in the Olympic hockey （冰球）. The World Cup is also chiefly responsible for sleep deprivation(剥夺）.The worst night for sleep in the U. K was the night of the England-Italy match on June 14. Brits stayed up a half-hour later to watch it, and then they woke up earlier than usual the next morning thanks to summer nights, the phenomenon in which the sun barely sets in northern countries in the summertime. That was nothing, though, compared to Germans, Italians, and the French, who stayed up around an hour and a half later on various days throughout the summer to watch the Cup.
paragraphs.translationZh: 同样，美国人的深夜、清晨和最长的睡眠时间都发生在三天的周末。加拿大队在奥运会曲棍球比赛中击败瑞典队的那一晚，成为了今年睡眠最少的国家。世界杯也是造成睡眠不足的主要原因。英国睡眠质量最差的一晚是6月14日英格兰与意大利的比赛当晚。英国人晚了半个小时才熬夜观看比赛，然后由于夏夜，北方国家夏季太阳几乎不落山的现象，他们第二天早上比平常起得更早。不过，与德国人、意大利人和法国人熬夜大约一个小时左右相比，这不算什么。整个夏天的不同日子都可以观看半年后的杯赛。

paragraphs.sourceText: It should be made clear that not everyone has a device to record their sleep patterns; in some of these nations, it’s likely that only the richest people do. And people who elect to track their sleep may try to get more sleep than the average person. Even if that’s the case, though, the above findings are still striking. If the most health-conscious among us have such deep swings in our shut-eye levels throughout the year, how much sleep are the rest of us losing?
paragraphs.translationZh: 应该明确的是，并不是每个人都有记录睡眠模式的设备；在其中一些国家，可能只有最富有的人才会这样做。选择追踪睡眠的人可能会尝试比普通人获得更多的睡眠。但即便如此，上述发现仍然令人震惊。如果我们当中最注重健康的人全年的睡眠水平波动如此之大，那么我们其他人会损失多少睡眠呢？
